[AGENT]: Welcome to Meridian Corp, Jamie! It's completely normal to feel a bit lost on day one — that's exactly what I'm here for. Let me look up the time off policy for you right now.Great news — here's how time off works at Meridian Corp:

**PTO (Paid Time Off)**
- You get **20 days of paid time off per year** — this covers vacation, personal days, etc., all in one bucket.
- It **accrues gradually**: about **1.67 days per month**, so you'll build it up as you go rather than having it all available upfront.

**A few important things to know:**
- ⚠️ **PTO does not roll over.** Any unused days are forfeited on **December 31st**, so make sure to use what you've earned by year-end.
- You need to **request PTO at least 2 business days in advance** (emergencies are the exception).
- Requests are submitted through the **HR portal at hr.meridian.com**.

**Quick tip for day one:** Since you just started, you've already started accruing for this month — but it'll be a small amount, so don't worry about rushing to use it. Just good to know it's building!

Is there anything else you'd like to know — benefits, payroll, equipment, or anything else? Happy to help you get settled. 😊

[AGENT]: You've got it exactly right! The math can feel a little confusing at first, but your instinct is correct. Here's a simple way to think about it:

**How accrual works in plain English:**
- The 20 days are spread evenly across the year — you earn roughly **1.67 days at the end of each month**.
- So you don't start with 20 days in the bank. You *build up to* 20 days over the course of the full year.

**Your specific situation (starting today):**
Since you just started, here's roughly what you'd have available:

| After... | Approx. PTO available |
|---|---|
| 1 month | ~1.67 days |
| 2 months | ~3.33 days |
| 3 months | ~5 days |
| 6 months | ~10 days |

So if you wanted to take a **full week off next month**, you'd only have around **1–2 days** accrued by then — not quite enough for 5 days. You'd want to wait a few months to have a fuller balance built up.

**One thing I'd recommend clarifying:** The policy doesn't specify whether you can take PTO *in advance* of accruing it (sometimes called "going negative"). That's worth a quick check with HR directly — you can reach them at **hr@meridian.com**.

But overall — yes, you understood it perfectly! Any other questions? 😊

That way they have all the context they need to give you a clear answer quickly. 😊

**The math:**
